questions.explanation: Standard output redirection ('>') typically truncates the existing file to zero length. Therefore, it should be opened with O_TRUNC along with O_WRONLY and O_CREATE.
dup2 atomically replaces a standard file descriptor (like stdout 1 or stdin 0) with a target file descriptor, ensuring standard library calls or external processes write to or read from the file.
The filename token immediately following the redirection operator must be extracted and treated as the redirection target rather than being passed as a standard command argument.
If running built-in commands or maintaining a persistent shell loop, failing to restore standard descriptors means subsequent shell output or input will permanently target the redirected files.

challenges.title: Parse Output Redirection Operator
challenges.solution: func ParseRedirection(tokens []string) ([]string, string) { var args []string; var outFile string; for i := 0; i < len(tokens); i++ { if tokens[i] == ">" && i+1 < len(tokens) { outFile = tokens[i+1] i++ } else { args = append(args, tokens[i]) } } return args, outFile }

challenges.title: Configuring File Redirection for Commands
challenges.solution: file, err := os.OpenFile(filename, os.O_CREATE|os.O_WRONLY|os.O_TRUNC, 0644); if err != nil { return err }; defer file.Close(); err = syscall.Dup2(int(file.Fd()), int(os.Stdout.Fd())); if err != nil { return err }
